rules.title: Cartwright Act amendments on common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
rules.requirement: Bars using or distributing a common pricing algorithm (a methodology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) if the person coerces another to adopt the algorithm's recommended price or term. A secondary source adds a ban on using or distributing such algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade. The law is not specific to rental housing. It does not limit other antitrust law.
rules.key_value: Civil fines up to $1 million in cases brought by the Attorney General or a district attorney (secondary source); effective Jan. 1, 2026

coverage.summary: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm, including in apartment rental pricing. It is a general antitrust rule, not limited to housing. It does not reach businesses that use proprietary algorithms with only their own data.
coverage.other_conditions: Algorithm must be used by two or more persons and use competitor data.

rules.exemptions: Proprietary algorithms using only the business's own data are not affected (secondary source).
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date comes from a secondary law-firm source stating AB 325 and SB 763 took effect January 1, 2026.
citation_aliases: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code ch. 2 (Cartwright Act)
rules.quoted_span: to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
rules.review_note: The official passage is truncated and does not give the codified section number or the full prohibition text. Effective date, penalty and the restraint-of-trade prong come from a secondary source.
rules.source_notes: Berkeley, San Diego and San Francisco passages describe city ordinances and are excluded from this state-level record.
